public_rationale: The dated record documents recurring autonomy predictions from 2014 through 2022. Tesla's own quarterly disclosure and September release instructions identify FSD as beta and require the driver to remain attentive at all times. That supports the ordinary reading of Marcus's statement. The promises had different horizons; the evidence does not imply that every annual statement promised delivery the following year.
limitations: Several historical promises are documented through contemporaneous journalism or a retrospective chronology rather than original recordings.
Tesla's historical disclosure and release instructions were accessed through third-party reproductions.
This assessment concerns the software available before the post, not subsequent Tesla developments.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Tesla's driverless car project, promised nearly yearly since 2014, is still in beta and is not really a driverless car, as it requires constant driver attention.

statement.excerpt: He been promising driverless cars pretty much ever year since 2014 and still hasn’t yet gotten that project out of beta, and the thing that is in beta isn’t still isn’t really a driverless car at all, so much as a car that can drive for you some of the time, provided you pay really strict attention all of the time.
statement.document_title: Top 5 reasons Tesla’s Optimus announcement may turn out be a dud

from_speaker: still hasn’t yet gotten that project out of beta
provided you pay really strict attention all of the time
our_interpretation: 'Pretty much every year' means a sustained, approximately annual pattern of public predictions about eventual driverless capability; it does not require an identical promise or deadline every year.
The historical promise component covers 2014 through the post date.
For the ongoing software-status component, use the latest publicly documented release before the post, in September 2022.
'Driverless' means operation without a human continuously supervising and remaining ready to intervene.
criteria.support_condition: Dated records establish approximately annual driverless predictions beginning in 2014, while contemporary Tesla software documentation identifies FSD as beta and requires continuous driver attention.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The historical record lacks the claimed recurring predictions, or Tesla had released the relevant system for operation without continuous driver supervision before the post.

evidence.excerpt: Full auto-pilot capability is going to happen, probably, in the five- or six-year time frame.
evidence.locator: Paragraph 2, quotation attributed to Musk's Nikkei interview
evidence.explanation: Documents a public prediction of full autonomy in 2014. Its horizon was five or six years, so it does not support the stronger claim that Musk promised delivery the following year in every instance.

evidence.excerpt: Musk says during the first earnings call of the year he expects full self-driving by the end of 2019.
evidence.locator: A Comprehensive Timeline of Elon Musk’s Autonomy Timelines, January 2019 entry
evidence.explanation: The quoted entry records the 2019 prediction. The same chronology documents full-autonomy predictions in 2015, the proposed autonomous cross-country drive in 2016 and 2017, and renewed autonomy predictions in 2018.

evidence.excerpt: Tesla will be able to make its vehicles completely autonomous by the end of this year, founder Elon Musk has said.
evidence.explanation: Documents a 2020 prediction explicitly concerning autonomy without driver input.

evidence.excerpt: I would be shocked if we do not achieve full self-driving safer than human this year.
evidence.locator: Opening section, Musk quotation; also REGULATION section for the preceding year's prediction
evidence.explanation: Records the January 2022 prediction. The article also quotes Musk's corresponding 2021 earnings-call prediction, completing the approximately annual sequence.

evidence.excerpt: As of the end of Q2-2022, over 100,000 Tesla drivers in North America had access to FSD Beta.
evidence.locator: Page 8, Core Technology, Autopilot and Full Self-Driving
evidence.explanation: Tesla's latest completed-quarter disclosure before the post identified the customer program as FSD Beta and described its operation as supervised.

evidence.excerpt: Keep your hands on the wheel and remain attentive at all times.
evidence.publisher: Tesla release instructions, reproduced by Not a Tesla App
evidence.explanation: The September FSD Beta release instructions explicitly require continuous attention. The release's availability by September 20 is independently corroborated by the contemporaneous TechCrunch report considered above.
